_meta.note: Values from ESP-IDF "GPIO & RTC GPIO" (stable) and Espressif datasheets; contradictions are listed in notes. conditional_pins are only occupied depending on the module (PSRAM/octal/SiP flash).

esp32.name: ESP32
esp32.cpu: Xtensa LX6 dual-core up to 240 MHz (ESP32-S0WD: single-core, 160 MHz)

strapping_pins.0: Boot mode (weak pull-up, 1): 1 = SPI boot, 0 (+GPIO2=0) = download boot (UART/SDIO)
strapping_pins.2: Boot mode (pull-down, 0): must be 0 for download boot
strapping_pins.5: SDIO slave timing together with MTDO (pull-up, 1)
strapping_pins.12: MTDI: VDD_SDIO voltage (pull-down, 0): 0 = 3.3 V, 1 = 1.8 V internal LDO; can be overridden via eFuse EFUSE_SDIO_FORCE
strapping_pins.15: MTDO: U0TXD ROM output (pull-up, 1 = on) and SDIO slave timing

notes: GPIO34-39 input-only, no software-enabled pull-up/pull-down
GPIO6-11 and GPIO16-17 are connected to SPI flash/PSRAM on modules – do not use
ADC2 unusable while Wi-Fi is active – use ADC1 (GPIO32-39)
GPIO12 (MTDI) sets the VDD_SDIO voltage at reset: an external pull-up with 3.3 V flash causes boot problems
Do not use GPIO36/GPIO39 interrupts while ADC or Wi-Fi/BT with sleep is active (errata GPIO-3.11)
Per datasheet, the touch sensor did not pass the conducted susceptibility (CS) test; limited use
No native USB; flashing via UART0 (GPIO1/GPIO3)
RTC-RAM: 8 KB RTC FAST + 8 KB RTC SLOW
Touch mapping per datasheet: T0=GPIO4, T1=GPIO0, T2=GPIO2, T3=GPIO15, T4=GPIO13, T5=GPIO12, T6=GPIO14, T7=GPIO27, T8=GPIO33, T9=GPIO32

conditional_pins.16: PSRAM (SPI0/1) on WROVER/PSRAM modules, free on WROOM without PSRAM
conditional_pins.17: PSRAM (SPI0/1) on WROVER/PSRAM modules, free on WROOM without PSRAM

12: HIGH at reset ⇒ flash voltage 1.8 V – 3.3 V flash then fails to boot (typically: "flash read err"). Do not connect a pull-up.

esp32s2.name: ESP32-S2
esp32s2.cpu: Xtensa LX7 single-core up to 240 MHz

strapping_pins.0: Boot mode (weak pull-up, 1): 1 = SPI boot, 0 (+GPIO46=0) = joint download boot (USB-OTG/UART/SPI)
strapping_pins.45: VDD_SPI voltage (weak pull-down, 0): 0 = 3.3 V, 1 = 1.8 V; can be overridden via eFuse
strapping_pins.46: Boot mode with GPIO0 and ROM output (weak pull-down, 0); input-only

notes: No Bluetooth
No USB-Serial-JTAG controller, only USB-OTG (full-speed) on GPIO19/20
GPIO26-32 reserved for SPI flash/PSRAM
GPIO46 input-only, fixed pull-down
ADC2 is shared with Wi-Fi (the IDF driver arbitrates access)
JTAG on GPIO39-42

esp32s3.name: ESP32-S3
esp32s3.cpu: Xtensa LX7 dual-core up to 240 MHz

strapping_pins.0: Boot mode (weak pull-up, 1): 1 = SPI boot, 0 (+GPIO46=0) = joint download boot (USB-Serial-JTAG/USB-OTG/UART)
strapping_pins.3: JTAG signal source (floating, no internal pulls) – only effective with EFUSE_STRAP_JTAG_SEL
strapping_pins.45: VDD_SPI voltage (weak pull-down, 0): 0 = 3.3 V, 1 = 1.8 V; can be overridden via eFuse
strapping_pins.46: Boot mode with GPIO0 and ROM output (weak pull-down, 0)

notes: GPIO26-32 reserved for SPI flash/PSRAM; with octal flash/PSRAM additionally GPIO33-37
GPIO19/20 are USB-Serial-JTAG by default (also USB-OTG); reconfiguring them as GPIO disables USB-JTAG
ADC2 is shared with Wi-Fi (the IDF driver arbitrates access)
No DAC
GPIO3 as JTAG strapping pin is floating and has no internal pulls
Bluetooth LE only (Bluetooth 5, Mesh), no Classic BT
Datasheet variants with octal PSRAM: ESP32-S3R8, ESP32-S3R16V, ESP32-S3R8V (EOL)

conditional_pins.33: occupied with octal flash/octal PSRAM (SPIIO4-7, SPIDQS), e.g. ESP32-S3R8/R8V
conditional_pins.34: occupied with octal flash/octal PSRAM (SPIIO4-7, SPIDQS), e.g. ESP32-S3R8/R8V
conditional_pins.35: occupied with octal flash/octal PSRAM (SPIIO4-7, SPIDQS), e.g. ESP32-S3R8/R8V
conditional_pins.36: occupied with octal flash/octal PSRAM (SPIIO4-7, SPIDQS), e.g. ESP32-S3R8/R8V
conditional_pins.37: occupied with octal flash/octal PSRAM (SPIIO4-7, SPIDQS), e.g. ESP32-S3R8/R8V

esp32c2.name: ESP32-C2 (ESP8684)

strapping_pins.8: ROM output; 1 for joint download boot (no default pull, N/A)
strapping_pins.9: Boot mode (weak pull-up, 1): 1 = SPI boot, 0 (+GPIO8=1) = joint download boot (UART)

notes: Datasheet published under the name ESP8684 (esp32-c2_datasheet_en.pdf does not exist)
Chip has 21 GPIOs (GPIO0-20); only 14 usable on SiP flash variants – per ESP8684 datasheet: 14 GPIOs
Contradiction in the IDF page: the introduction lists GPIO11-17 for SiP flash, the table/note lists GPIO12-17 as SPI0/1
Only GPIO0-5 wake from deep sleep; the others only from light sleep
No native USB, no touch, no DAC, ADC1 only
BLE: datasheet states Bluetooth 5.3 certified
SRAM: 272 KB, of which 16 KB used as cache
not verified: RTC memory size (datasheet only states that RTC memory stays powered in deep sleep)

conditional_pins.11: reserved for flash on SiP flash variants (per IDF introduction; not marked as SPI0/1 in the IDF table)

strapping_pins.9: Boot mode (weak pull-up, 1): 1 = SPI boot, 0 (+GPIO8=1) = joint download boot (USB-Serial-JTAG/UART)

notes: GPIO12-17 reserved for SPI flash
GPIO18/19 are USB-Serial-JTAG by default; reconfiguring them as GPIO disables USB-JTAG
ADC2 (GPIO5) not supported by ESP-IDF in oneshot mode (unstable results, errata); can be forced via CONFIG_ADC_ONESHOT_FORCE_USE_ADC2_ON_C3
not verified: ADC2/Wi-Fi conflict – the C3 ADC page does not mention it, hence null
Only GPIO0-5 wake from deep sleep; the others only from light sleep
22 GPIOs for ESP32-C3/C3FH4/C3FN4/C3FH8X, only 16 for ESP32-C3FH4X and C3FH4AZ (datasheet)
SRAM: 400 KB, of which 16 KB used as cache
No touch, no DAC

5: ADC2 on ESP32-C3: oneshot operation not supported in ESP-IDF due to hardware errata – use ADC1 (GPIO0–4).

esp8266.name: ESP8266 (ESP8266EX)
esp8266.cpu: Tensilica L106 32-bit single-core up to 160 MHz

strapping_pins.0: Boot mode: low = ROM serial bootloader (download), high = boot from flash
strapping_pins.2: must be high (pull-up or open, internal weak pull-up); in download mode the ROM outputs UART TX on GPIO2

notes: ADC: only one 10-bit SAR ADC on pin TOUT (pin 6, not a GPIO, often A0 on modules); input range 0-1.0 V; alternatively measures VDD3P3 – not both at the same time
Connect GPIO16 (XPD_DCDC) to EXT_RSTB for deep-sleep wake; GPIO16 has only an internal pull-down, the other GPIOs only a pull-up
GPIO6-11 connected to SPI flash – do not use
GPIO0, GPIO2, GPIO15 (MTDO) form the 3-bit strapping for boot and SDIO mode
U0TXD must not be pulled low externally at power-on
UART0 can be swapped to GPIO15 (TX/RTS) and GPIO13 (RX/CTS)
jtag_pins = pin names per datasheet; not verified: JTAG debug support
not verified: total SRAM and RTC RAM size (datasheet only states approx. 50 kB heap+data in station mode)
Chip is NRND per datasheet, recommended successor ESP8684 (ESP32-C2)
Wi-Fi 802.11 b/g/n, HT20 only; no Bluetooth; no native USB

16: GPIO16 (XPD_DCDC): no interrupts, no internal pull-up (pull-down only); connect to RST for deep-sleep wake.
1: TX0 – boot log and serial; active during boot.
